doc.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018

chapter: Howard Johnson and the loft scene
title: Latin gigs on valve trombone and meeting Howard Johnson
summary: Rowe asks about a path into jazz; Daley describes Latin scene work and encountering Howard Johnson.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well it’s quite a leap from that to the loft scene. And I wondered, as a tuba player, if you started listening to jazz, what did you think that your pathway into that music could be? Because you’re not hearing a lot of tubas unless you’re listening to New Orleans early, really early stuff, or I guess the opportunity presented by this new music.

Yeah most definitely. So again, like mentors and stuff, people that you run into that change your life and change your course in history. So in New York City like I said, I grew up on the Latin, you know, New York scene, on the lower east side, which was a big Latin mecca. So I was playing — I had a valve trombone that I was doing gigs on on the Latin scene, playing valve trombones. And during the weekend the Latin scene, you can do a gig, an early gig starting around maybe eight, then you move to another venue and do a late night gig, and then you do an after-hours club until the next morning. Because that was before D.J.s and all that kind of thing. So every time you went into a club it was live music. Either Latin music or rhythm & blues. People came to dance to a real band. Unlike now when you come in and the guys are doing all kinds of stuff with the records and everything. So you can definitely work. So I worked a lot you know, but the concept of me playing tuba or anything in that context was like foreign to me because there was no other example. I didn’t see any other tuba player playing in these bands. But then I ran into the great Howard Johnson. He was one of my — he kind of turned my whole concept around about what tuba can do.
